correctness.rationale: At any x, the data-increment representation is a convex combination of the two constant vertices and three steps. For the Lobatto grid, the terminal step (x+1)(4x²−1)/6 has minimum −(10+7√7)/162 at x=(√7−2)/6; its other critical point has positive value and its maximum is 1. The middle-step defect is 7√21/54−1/2, strictly smaller. Unique minimization over vertices and x gives the unique lower data/location pair, and reflection with complementation gives the upper pair. Mixing either step with any strictly increasing admissible vector proves approachability. For the uniform grid the terminal step is (9/16)u(u²−4/9), u=x+1/3, with undershoot √3/27; the middle step is 1/2+[(13/9)x−x³]/(8/9), with minimum at −√39/9 and larger defect 13√39/108−1/2. Independent cardinal evaluation and derivative-root enumeration corroborated both grids. The exact argument, not floating-point comparisons, establishes strictness and uniqueness.
